title: Jahanabad Buddha
subtitle: Manglawar rock relief up the Malam Jabba road, Lower Swat

landmark.name: Jahanabad Buddha
edits: The boulder is the Atlas's procedural model: a rounded granite mass about 12 x 11 x 9 m, flattened on the carved face and sunk 1 m into the slope; its size, lumps and weathering tones are estimated (no survey).

The Buddha in relief is drawn to the published size: the carved figure is 7 m high and 5 m wide (700 x 500 cm), its throne 1.2 m high and 3.9 m wide (120 x 390 cm); the relief stands 0.11 m proud of the niche floor. The oval niche (about 8.8 x 8.4 m) and its depth of 0.3 m are estimated. The folds, hands, head and halo are estimated from the published description and the photos.
The figure's foot is set 1 m above the ground at the face (estimated).
Trees within 25 m of the carving are left out so it can be seen; WorldCover maps tree cover there. A timber viewing deck (about 3.6 x 1.5 m) and a few boulders in front are estimated from the photos.
No steps are mapped in OSM and none show in the photos, so none are drawn; the walk up from the road is traced over the ground (easiest slope on the DEM).
The carving is drawn restored and without the 2007 damage to the head.

sources.name: Buddhist rock carving in Manglawar (Wikipedia)
